questions.q: What happens when you add a duplicate item to a set?
options: The set doubles the existing item's value
It raises an error immediately
Nothing — sets automatically drop duplicates, so the set stays the same size
It silently converts the set into a list
questions.explain: A set guarantees every item is unique; adding something already present has no effect.

questions.q: What does `team_a & team_b` return, if both are sets?
options: The union of both sets
This is invalid syntax for sets
The difference — only items in team_a
The intersection — only items present in both sets
questions.explain: The & operator on sets returns the intersection: items that appear in both.

questions.q: Why does `coordinates[0] = 41.0` raise a TypeError if coordinates is a tuple?
options: Tuples don't actually raise this error; it would work fine
Because index 0 doesn't exist in any tuple
Because tuples are immutable — once created, their contents can't be reassigned
Because tuples can only hold strings, not numbers
questions.explain: Tuples are immutable, so attempting to assign to an index raises a TypeError, unlike a list.

questions.q: Why can a tuple be used as a dictionary key while a list cannot?
options: There's no real difference — both work equally well as keys
Because dictionaries only accept string keys
Because lists are too large to be used as keys
Because dictionary keys must be immutable, and tuples are immutable while lists are not
questions.explain: Python requires dictionary keys to be immutable (hashable); tuples qualify, but lists, being mutable, do not.

questions.q: Which structure would you reach for to automatically remove duplicate values from a list of model names?
options: There is no structure in Python that handles this
A dictionary, since dictionaries cannot contain duplicates
A set — converting the list with set(my_list) drops duplicates automatically
A tuple, since tuples cannot contain duplicates
questions.explain: Converting a list to a set is the standard, idiomatic way to de-duplicate its values in Python.
